PullRequest.Title: chat: simplify Discover intro and search guidance
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Make the Discover introduction calmer and more benefit-led, with a single documentation link instead of six competing customization-type links.

- Subtitle: “Tailor your agent to your tools, your team, and your workflow. Learn more”
- Link “Learn more” to https://aka.ms/vscode-customizations, with a descriptive screen-reader label.
- Search placeholder: “Search MCP servers, plugins, skills and more...” to introduce customization concepts quietly, following the Copilot app reference.
- Keep the existing heading, sidebar navigation, and search behavior unchanged.
- Update focused unit tests and the component fixture assertion.

No linked issue; this is a UX copy refinement.

## UX review

No actionable findings in the final UX-focused review. Checked the final copy in dark/default and light/narrow component screenshots: the subtitle wraps without clipping and the single link remains discoverable. Verified that the short link resolves to VS Code’s agent-customization documentation. The link retains native keyboard focusability and a descriptive accessible name.

## Validation

Run with the repository-required Node 24.18.0 (the system Node 24.0 does not execute the current `import.meta.main` entry points):

- `npm.cmd exec --yes --package=node@24.18.0 -- node build\next\build-fast.ts --client-only` — passed; final client output refreshed.
- `npm.cmd exec --yes --package=node@24.18.0 -- cmd.exe /d /c ".\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\aiCustomizationDiscoveryPage.test.ts --reporter dot"` — passed, 79 tests.
- `npm.cmd exec --yes --package=node@24.18.0 -- node build\eslint.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\aiCustomization\aiCustomizationDiscoveryPage.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\aiCustomizationDiscoveryPage.test.ts src\vs\workbench\test\browser\componentFixtures\sessions\aiCustomizationManagementEditor.fixture.ts` — passed, all three changed files.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Component Explorer screenshots: `DiscoverWithMcpGalleryOnly/Dark` and `DiscoverSearchResultsNarrow/Light` — rendered successfully and visually reviewed with final copy.

Full type-check, smoke/integration suites, and live screen-reader testing were not run for this localized copy/link change.

## How to test

1. Enable the Customization Marketplace and open Discover in Agent Customizations.
2. Confirm the benefit-led subtitle contains only one link, “Learn more”.
3. Activate the link and confirm it opens the customization documentation.
4. Confirm the empty search field mentions MCP servers, plugins, and skills; search and sidebar navigation should behave as before.
5. Narrow the editor and confirm the subtitle wraps cleanly.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Agent Customizations Discover page
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The constructor synchronously renders the heading, description, and search widget; visibility then starts the existing catalog load when the browse cache is cold. The changed description is on the synchronous UI path but now creates one anchor/listener instead of six.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the customization marketplace for the initial catalog page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for a cold initial browse; zero on a warm browse-cache hit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cold/warm marketplace query behavior existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Controls catalog population but is independent of description and placeholder rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant-size localized header text and links; catalog results scale with the existing configured page size, independently of the copy change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Description rendering is synchronous. Catalog loading permits one active request owned by the page, cancelling the prior request before starting another.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing browseCatalogCache avoids the marketplace query for a warm empty-query/source selection. The description itself has no cache and is rendered once per page instance; the diff reduces its DOM/listener cardinality.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the constructor call, formatted-text renderer, disposable listener ownership, cache lookup, and marketplace query path were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact DOM timing and marketplace latency vary, but the changed synchronous work is smaller than before and does not alter request count.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: page-load DOM nodes and listeners decrease from six links to one, cleanup remains owned by descriptionDisposables, and catalog I/O is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate the new Learn more documentation link
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A discrete click prevents default navigation and asynchronously invokes IOpenerService; browser builds use an external window and desktop builds cross the native-host boundary to launch the configured/default browser. The callback does not await this operation before returning to the UI event loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: On desktop, request the native host to open the external documentation URL, potentially launching a browser process; browser builds call window.open instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one boundary call per Learn more activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each of the six former description links selected a local customization section and did not open an external resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to fulfill the explicit external-navigation action; it is not on Discover page load, rendering, typing, or catalog-loading critical paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One opener invocation per explicit user activation; there is no collection-driven or lifecycle-driven multiplicity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No coalescing is present, so separate clicks can create separate opener calls, but concurrency is bounded by discrete user gestures rather than automatic fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved; any browser or redirect caching occurs outside this feature and does not affect invocation cardinality.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed callback, openExternal helper, opener service, and desktop/browser default opener implementations were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External browser launch latency depends on platform and browser state, but the operation is deliberate, one-shot, and user requested.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new boundary is the requested semantics of a single documentation link, occurs only on explicit activation, and has no realistic scaling or hot-path trigger.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type in the Discover search field and load marketplace results
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Typing flows through the existing input-change handler, render, RunOnceScheduler, cancellation, and marketplace query path. The diff changes only placeholder text and adds no work to input events or result processing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the customization marketplace after the existing search delay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active query after coalescing for ordinary searches; existing bounded sequential backfill may fetch additional pages for unsupported combined type filters.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical scheduler, cancellation, query, pagination, and cache behavior with the former placeholder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines result availability, but its scheduling and cardinality are unchanged by the placeholder copy.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Search request work continues to scale with typed query changes after scheduler coalescing and, for existing filtered backfill, a bounded sequential page count; the placeholder length is constant.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing scheduler coalesces input changes and loadCatalog cancels the prior request before issuing the next; backfill pages are sequential.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Empty browse queries can reuse browseCatalogCache; non-empty searches follow the existing request path. The copy change alters neither cache keys, hits, misses, nor invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line and the transitive input, scheduler, cancellation, cache, and query paths were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual result sizes and network latency vary, but there is no changed mechanism affecting them.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the longer placeholder is constant-size display text and does not change search execution, network fan-out, allocation scaling, or concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and every diff page. The production change replaces six description links with one, changes constant copy, and adds one user-triggered external opener call; no hot-path, scaling, retention, cache, concurrency, or boundary-fanout regression meets the reporting threshold.
